learn.title: Small Wind Turbines for Homes
learn.intro: Small wind turbines generate clean electricity for homes and communities, reducing reliance on fossil fuels. They harness wind energy to power appliances, cut bills, and support energy independence, especially in rural or off-grid areas.
learn.c1_text: Turbines convert wind kinetic energy into electricity via spinning blades and generators. A 10 kW turbine can power a small home, generating ~10,000 kWh/year in windy regions.
learn.c2_text: Turbines need consistent wind speeds (12+ m/s). Urban areas face turbulence; rural sites with open land are ideal. Proper placement boosts efficiency by up to 20%.
learn.c3_text: India has 30% untapped wind potential. Small turbines can serve remote villages, aligning with PM Surya Ghar's goal of 300 GW renewable energy by 2030.
learn.stat2: Global small wind market to hit $3.5B by 2030
learn.stat3: Turbines reduce grid demand by 15-30% in optimal sites
learn.stat4: Payback period: 5-15 years depending on location

learn.title: Agrivoltaics: Farming + Solar
learn.intro: Agrivoltaics combines solar panels with crop farming, maximizing land use. This dual-use system boosts renewable energy adoption while supporting food security and biodiversity.
learn.c1_text: Solar panels elevated above crops allow sunlight and rain to reach plants. Studies show tomato yields increased by 16% under panels due to microclimate benefits.
learn.c2_text: Panels tilt at 30-40° to balance energy capture and crop growth. Bifacial panels capture reflected light, increasing energy output by 10-15% compared to ground-mounted systems.
learn.c3_text: India's first agrivoltaic project in Karnataka uses 1 MW solar + 500 fruit trees. The government aims to install 1 GW agrivoltaics by 2025 under the National Solar Mission.
learn.stat2: Global agrivoltaics market to reach $3.2B by 2027
learn.stat3: Water use reduced by 20-30% in agrivoltaic systems
learn.stat4: Farmers earn 20-30% higher income from dual revenue streams

learn.title: Battery Management Systems
learn.intro: BMS protect batteries in EVs and grids by monitoring temperature, voltage, and charge cycles. They extend battery life, prevent failures, and optimize performance for renewable energy systems.
learn.c1_text: BMS equalize charge across cells. A 95% charged cell won't overcharge others, preventing 20% capacity loss over 5 years.
learn.c2_text: Lithium-ion batteries operate best at 20-25°C. BMS cools/heats cells, maintaining efficiency. Tesla's BMS keeps battery temps within 10-35°C, even in extreme climates.
learn.c3_text: India's EV battery market needs 100,000 BMS units annually. ISRO's BMS tech reduces thermal runaway risks by 90%, supporting PM E-Drive's 30% EV target by 2030.
learn.stat3: Thermal management cuts battery degradation by 40%
learn.stat4: EV battery recycling boosts BMS resale value by 15%

learn.title: Solar PV Photoelectric Effect
learn.intro: Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity using the photoelectric effect. Photons knock electrons free, creating current. This technology powers 4.5% of global electricity.
learn.c1_text: Silicon panels absorb photons, freeing electrons. A 1 m² panel generates 150W in direct sunlight, powering 1.5 LED bulbs continuously.
learn.c2_text: Electrons flow through wires to create DC current. Inverters convert DC to AC, matching grid voltage (230V in India). Efficiency ranges from 15-22% for commercial panels.
learn.c3_text: India has 70 GW solar installed (2024), ranking 3rd globally. The PLI Scheme offers 20% incentives for domestic solar cell manufacturing, creating 100,000 jobs.
learn.stat2: Global solar capacity to hit 1000 GW by 2030

learn.title: Capacity Factor Explained
learn.intro: Capacity factor measures how much energy a plant produces vs. its maximum potential. Solar averages 15-25%, wind 35-55%, showing why overbuilding renewables ensures reliable power.
learn.c1_text: A 100 MW solar plant with 20% capacity factor produces 1,825 GWh/year (vs. 8,760 GWh max). Wind farms in Tamil Nadu reach 45% capacity factor due to consistent monsoon winds.
learn.c2_text: Low capacity factors require grid storage or backup. India's 40 GW wind+solar hybrid projects use 4-hour storage to smooth output, reducing curtailment by 30%.
learn.c3_text: India's national average capacity factor is 22%. The Grid-Connected Renewable Energy Policy mandates 25%+ capacity factors for new projects to qualify for subsidies.

learn.title: Electric Buses & Trucks
learn.intro: Electric buses and trucks cut urban emissions by 50-70%. With 2.5M EVs on roads, India aims for 100% EV public transport by 2030, supported by battery swapping and charging networks.
learn.c1_text: Electric buses use 300-400 kWh batteries. A 200 kWh battery powers a Tata Starbus for 300 km, reducing fuel costs by ₹15,000/month vs. diesel.
learn.c2_text: DC fast chargers refill 80% in 30 mins. India's charging network has 15,000+ stations, with 40% in Tier 2 cities under FAME II subsidies.
learn.c3_text: India's EV30@30 plan targets 30% EV penetration by 2030. Delhi's 1,000 electric buses cut PM2.5 by 18%, saving ₹1,200 crores annually in healthcare costs.
learn.stat3: EV trucks cut CO2 by 1.5 tons/km vs. diesel
